strategy.angle: The shift from generative AI to high-throughput agentic infrastructure.
strategy.audience: Houston business leaders, CTOs, and operational executives.

draft.hook: Stop confusing chatbots with autonomous agents—the true infrastructure for scalable AI just arrived, and it renders your current pilot programs obsolete.
draft.body: NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3 Super, packed with a 120B parameter weight set but firing on just 12B active parameters, changes the math on enterprise deployment. Why does this matter for Houston’s core operations? It solves the latency-to-accuracy bottleneck that has kept AI from moving beyond email drafting into supply chain orchestration and automated refinery monitoring. Can this actually impact our bottom line? Yes. By dramatically increasing throughput while lowering inference costs, this architecture allows agents to make real-time decisions at a scale previously reserved for massive data centers. Through Amplify Intelligence, I am seeing that the companies preparing to integrate these efficient, agentic models into their existing stacks are the ones that will secure a 15-20% margin advantage over competitors still relying on standard, slower LLMs.
draft.closing: Leon Coe is watching the shift from 'AI as a tool' to 'AI as an autonomous workforce.' The technology is no longer the risk; the risk is the business strategy that fails to account for this leap in model efficiency.
draft.cta: If you are ready to pivot your AI strategy from experimental cost-centers to autonomous revenue-drivers, message me to review your deployment roadmap.
